Forecasting Crude Oil Price with Probabilistic Graphical Models¶

MScFE 660 — Risk Management — Group Work Project 1¶

  • Student A (macroeconomic / geopolitical) -> FRED API (fredapi, uses your free key): WTI (WTISPLC), CPI-U (CPIAUCSL), IMF global energy price index (PNRGINDEXM), Saudi oil production (SAUNGDPMOMBD).
  • Student C (financial) -> Yahoo Finance (yfinance, no key): S&P 500 (^GSPC), volatility index (^VIX), 10-year Treasury yield (^TNX).

Group of two: the microeconomic role (Student B) is eliminated per the brief.

import yfinance as yf
YF = {"SP500":"^GSPC","VIX":"^VIX","TNX":"^TNX"}
def yclose(tkr):
    d = yf.download(tkr, period="max", interval="1d", auto_adjust=True, progress=False)
    c = d["Close"]
    return (c.iloc[:,0] if hasattr(c,"columns") else c)
fin = {name: yclose(tkr).rename(name) for name,tkr in YF.items()}

raw = {**macro, **fin}

# monthly grid: FRED monthly series as-is; annual Saudi supply forward-filled;
# daily Yahoo prices aggregated to monthly means
freq={"WTI":"m","CPI":"m","ENERGY":"m","SAUDI":"f","SP500":"m","VIX":"m","TNX":"m"}
def monthly(s,how):
    s=s.sort_index().resample("MS").mean()
    return s.ffill() if how=="f" else s
panel=pd.DataFrame({k:monthly(v,freq[k]) for k,v in raw.items()})
print("Combined monthly panel before windowing:", panel.shape)

Steps 5 & 6 - Cleaning the sterilised dataset¶

Passes: (A) trim to common window and flag implausible >60% month-on-month moves on price/index series; (B) treat non-positive levels as invalid; (C) impute internal gaps by time interpolation. Slower/annual series are forward-filled rather than dropped.

In [5]:
START,END="2000-01-01","2025-12-01"
df=panel.loc[START:END].copy(); log={}
log["nonpositive"]=int((df<=0).sum().sum()); df=df.mask(df<=0)
log["gaps_imputed"]=int(df.isna().sum().sum()); df=df.interpolate(method="time",limit_direction="both")
for c in ["WTI","ENERGY","SP500"]:
    df.loc[df[c].pct_change().abs()>0.60,c]=np.nan
df=df.interpolate(method="time",limit_direction="both").dropna()
print("Sterilised panel:",df.shape,"| window",df.index.min().date(),"->",df.index.max().date())
print(log); df.describe().round(2)

Answers. (a) Oil differs from equities through violent, geopolitically-driven price spikes (2008 super-spike, 2014-16 shale collapse, 2020 COVID crash, 2022 Russia-Ukraine surge), volatility clustering and persistent bull/bear regimes. (b) Returns are fat-tailed and left-skewed (skew ~ -1.00, excess kurtosis ~ 7.6); Jarque-Bera rejects normality (p ~ 2.6e-176). (c) Raw returns show weak memory (lag-1 ~ 0.27); absolute returns are strongly autocorrelated (lag-1 ~ 0.50; Ljung-Box p ~ 3.6e-22) - volatility clustering. (d) The level is highly persistent (ADF p ~ 0.03) while returns are stationary (ADF p ~ 4.7e-19), motivating first-differencing.

Regime detection with Hidden Markov Models¶

Each genuinely monthly series is turned into up/down emissions; a 3-state Categorical HMM is fit by Baum-Welch, decoded by Viterbi, and its states labelled bear / stagnant / bull by mean monthly change. The annual Saudi-supply series is discretised into terciles of its 12-month change.

In [10]:
def fit_hmm(series):
    X=(series.diff().dropna()>0).astype(int).values.reshape(-1,1)
    m=hmm.CategoricalHMM(n_components=3,n_iter=200,random_state=7,tol=1e-4); m.fit(X)
    _,s=m.decode(X); dv=series.diff().dropna().values
    order=pd.Series(dv).groupby(pd.Series(s)).mean().sort_values().index.tolist()
    remap={o:i for i,o in enumerate(order)}
    return pd.Series([remap[x] for x in s],index=series.diff().dropna().index)
def tercile(s): return pd.qcut(s,3,labels=[0,1,2],duplicates="drop").astype("float")
wti_reg=fit_hmm(df["WTI"])
disc=pd.DataFrame(index=df.index)
for c in ["WTI","ENERGY","CPI","SP500","VIX","TNX"]: disc[c]=fit_hmm(df[c])
disc["SAUDI"]=tercile(np.log(df["SAUDI"]).diff(12))
disc["forecast"]=wti_reg.shift(-1); disc=disc[PRED+["forecast"]].dropna().astype(int)
print("WTI regime counts (0 bear,1 stagnant,2 bull):"); print(disc["WTI"].value_counts().sort_index())

def regime_plot(dates,price,reg,title):
    fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(13,4.4)); cmap=ListedColormap(["#c0392b","#2c6fbb","#0b7a3b"])
    norm=BoundaryNorm(range(4),cmap.N); xn=mdates.date2num(dates.to_pydatetime())
    pts=np.array([xn,price]).T.reshape(-1,1,2); seg=np.concatenate([pts[:-1],pts[1:]],axis=1)
    lc=LineCollection(seg,cmap=cmap,norm=norm,lw=1.6); lc.set_array(reg[:-1]); ax.add_collection(lc)
    ax.set_xlim(xn.min(),xn.max()); ax.set_ylim(price.min()*.95,price.max()*1.03)
    ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.YearLocator(3)); ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%Y"))
    ax.set_xlabel("Date"); ax.set_ylabel("USD/bbl"); ax.set_title(title,weight="bold")
    ax.legend(handles=[mpatches.Patch(color="#c0392b",label="Bear"),mpatches.Patch(color="#2c6fbb",label="Stagnant"),
                       mpatches.Patch(color="#0b7a3b",label="Bull")],loc="upper left"); plt.show()
w=df.loc[wti_reg.index]; regime_plot(w.index,w["WTI"].values,wti_reg.values,"HMM-detected regimes in WTI crude oil")

Interpretation. The Viterbi path isolates bear collapses (2008-09, 2014-16, 2020) in red and bull runs in green. Mean monthly WTI change by regime: bear ~ $-4.93/bbl, stagnant ~ $1.39, bull ~ $3.71 - economically coherent before feeding the network.

def evaluate(b):
    yhat=model.predict(b.drop(columns=["forecast"]),n_jobs=1)["forecast"].values
    y=b["forecast"].values; return y,yhat,float(np.mean(y!=yhat))
yv,pv,ev=evaluate(va); yt,pt,et=evaluate(te)
base_v=float(np.mean(va["forecast"]!=va["WTI"])); base_t=float(np.mean(te["forecast"]!=te["WTI"]))
print(f"Validation accuracy {1-ev:.1%}   persistence baseline {1-base_v:.1%}")
print(f"Test accuracy       {1-et:.1%}   persistence baseline {1-base_t:.1%}")
print("Random 3-class accuracy ~= 33.3%")

Validation accuracy 60.0%   persistence baseline 26.7%
Test accuracy       73.3%   persistence baseline 40.0%

price=df.loc[te.index,"WTI"].values; _,sig,_=evaluate(te)
eq=[1.0]
for i in range(1,len(price)):
    r=price[i]/price[i-1]-1; s=sig[i-1]; pos=1 if s==2 else (-1 if s==0 else 0)
    eq.append(eq[-1]*(1+pos*r))
bh=price/price[0]
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(12,5))
ax.plot(te.index,eq,color=ACCENT,lw=2,label="Bayesian-network strategy"); ax.plot(te.index,bh,color="#444",lw=1.5,ls="--",label="Buy & hold WTI")
ax.set_xlabel("Date"); ax.set_ylabel("Growth of $1"); ax.set_title("Out-of-sample backtest (test window)",weight="bold"); ax.legend(); plt.show()
sr=np.diff(eq)/np.array(eq[:-1])
print(f"Strategy ${eq[-1]:.2f}  vs  buy&hold ${bh[-1]:.2f}   annualised Sharpe {np.mean(sr)/(np.std(sr)+1e-9)*np.sqrt(12):.2f}")

Strategy $1.80  vs  buy&hold $0.85   annualised Sharpe 1.50

Technical interpretation. Hill-climbing recovers an economically coherent DAG whose parents of forecast are CPI, inside a wider graph that links the energy complex, Saudi supply and the financial block (S&P 500, VIX, 10Y). Out-of-sample it forecasts the next-month WTI regime with 60.0% (validation) and 73.3% (test) accuracy - above the ~33% of random three-class guessing. Non-technical takeaway. Over the 2023-06-01-2025-11-01 test window (a falling oil market) the regime signal turned $1 into **$1.80** versus $0.85 for buy-and-hold (annualised Sharpe ~ 1.5) - value as a risk-management/hedging overlay, not a high-frequency alpha engine. (Small 30-month window - illustrative.)

Steps 9 & 10 - Model theory and Algorithm 1 (Inferred Causality)¶

The written theory (belief vs Markov networks; parameter vs structure learning; Markov chains and Markov blankets) and the Algorithm 1 pseudocode are in the accompanying report. In brief:

INFERRED CAUSALITY(data D over X1..Xm)
  Phase 1 - Markov blankets: learn B(Xi); drop asymmetric memberships
  Phase 2 - skeleton: if no S in min(B(Xi),B(Xj)) gives Xi _||_ Xj | S, add edge Xi-Xj
  Phase 3 - orient: v-structures Xi->Xk<-Xj for k not in Sep(Xi,Xj); apply Meek rules
  return CPDAG
